name: NGC 4302 and NGC 4298 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 4302 and NGC 4298, a close pair of spiral galaxies, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc4302-hubble
story: An edge-on spiral lies beside a tilted one, separated in projection by only about 7,000 light-years, yet neither shows the tidal tails and distortions that such close neighbors usually wear.

claims.text: NGC 4302 and NGC 4298 are spiral galaxies
NGC 4302 is seen edge-on and NGC 4298 is tilted
They are a close pair, separated in projection by about 7000 light-years
They lack the tidal tails and deformations typical of close galaxies
They form a close pair in the Virgo Cluster; program 14913 imaged them with WFC3/IR at this pointing
NASA released a Hubble WFC3 infrared image of the pair
